metadata.title: 1973 Case 12
metadata.original_presentation: A 50-year-old man was admitted to the hospital because of abdominal pain.

required.content: What is the patient's past medical history?
required.response: The patient had multiple small xanthomas on the elbows 21 years ago, intermittent claudication, episodes of blindness, high blood fat levels, recurrent abdominal pain, hiatus hernia, high cholesterol and triglycerides, and a history of chest pain. He underwent bilateral femoral endarterectomy and carotid artery exploration. He was treated with nicotinic acid, tolbutamide, warfarin, and clofibrate.

teaching_points.content: Xanthomas can be associated with hyperlipidemia and may indicate underlying metabolic disorders.
Intermittent claudication and episodes of transient blindness can be symptoms of peripheral vascular disease and carotid artery disease.
A history of high cholesterol and triglycerides is a risk factor for cardiovascular diseases.

required.content: What is the patient's family history?
required.response: The patient's mother died of arteriosclerosis and diabetes mellitus, maternal grandmother died of diabetes with xanthomas, several maternal cousins had diabetes, a brother died of arteriosclerosis, and a sister died of diabetes, arteriosclerosis, and liver disease.

teaching_points.content: Family history of diabetes and arteriosclerosis suggests a genetic predisposition to metabolic and cardiovascular diseases.

required.content: What are the patient's lifestyle factors?
required.response: The patient smoked three packages of cigarettes daily and consumed alcohol in excessive amounts in earlier years.

teaching_points.content: Smoking and excessive alcohol consumption are significant risk factors for cardiovascular and liver diseases.

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Familial Hypercholesterolemia
supporting_evidence: multiple small xanthomas on the elbows
family history of arteriosclerosis and xanthomas
additional_information_needed: genetic testing for LDL receptor mutations

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Atherosclerosis
supporting_evidence: bilateral femoral endarterectomy and carotid artery exploration

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Alcoholic Liver Disease
supporting_evidence: excessive alcohol consumption in earlier years

required.content: What were the findings on physical examination?
required.response: The patient appeared well except for evident abdominal pain. There was no icterus, a corneal arcus was seen bilaterally, normal jugular venous pressure, graded carotid pulsations, clear lungs, an S4 gallop sound, normal bowel sounds, tenderness in the epigastrium, and diminished distal pulses.

teaching_points.content: Corneal arcus can be associated with hyperlipidemia, especially in younger patients.
An S4 gallop sound may indicate left ventricular hypertrophy or decreased compliance.

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Familial Hypercholesterolemia
supporting_evidence: multiple small xanthomas on the elbows
family history of arteriosclerosis and xanthomas
additional_information_needed: Genetic testing for LDL receptor mutations

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Pancreatitis
supporting_evidence: excessive alcohol consumption in earlier years
refuting_evidence: No mention of elevated amylase or lipase levels

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Coronary Artery Disease
supporting_evidence: smoking three packages of cigarettes daily

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Diabetes Mellitus
key_features: history of high blood fat levels
refuting_evidence: No mention of hyperglycemia or diabetes diagnosis

required.content: What were the results of the laboratory tests?
required.response: The hematocrit was 45%, white-cell count 8400, urea nitrogen 16 mg, creatinine 1.4 mg, uric acid 6.4 mg, glucose 134 mg, conjugated bilirubin 0.3 mg, total bilirubin 0.8 mg, calcium 10.1 mg, phosphorus 3.3 mg, thyroxine 8.0 μg, protein 7.5 g, sodium 131 mEq, potassium 3.9 mEq, chloride 100 mEq, carbon dioxide 28 mEq, SGOT 185 U, LDH 170 U, CPK 30 U, lipase 1.0 U, amylase 8.0 U, alkaline phosphatase 3.3 Bodansky U.

teaching_points.content: Elevated SGOT and LDH can indicate liver damage or myocardial injury.

required.content: What imaging studies were performed and what were the findings?
required.response: An x-ray film of the chest was normal. An abdominal film showed vascular calcifications and phleboliths. An upper gastrointestinal series showed a large hiatus hernia and two calcified gallstones.

teaching_points.content: Vascular calcifications can be indicative of advanced atherosclerosis.

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Familial Hypercholesterolemia
supporting_evidence: history of high cholesterol and triglycerides
family history of arteriosclerosis and xanthomas
additional_information_needed: Genetic testing for LDL receptor mutations

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Hiatus Hernia
supporting_evidence: large hiatus hernia on upper gastrointestinal series

required.content: What treatments were administered during the hospital stay?
required.response: Clofibrate was omitted, and antacid, tincture of belladonna, and meperidine were administered. Clofibrate was resumed later, and pulmonary physical therapy was begun.

teaching_points.content: Clofibrate is used to lower cholesterol and triglyceride levels but may have side effects that require monitoring.

final_diagnosis.name: Complex metabolic and cardiovascular disorder
supporting_evidence: History of high cholesterol and triglycerides
Family history of diabetes and arteriosclerosis
Presence of corneal arcus and vascular calcifications
